results.label: this tree ships the M12 rule-break tally (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the vocabulary is the audit’s own kinds: a prevented attempt, an accepted override, an observed condition, a legal record
breaks are the ATTEMPTS: five prevented entries and one accepted override, not the conditions
a live stop state is reported SEPARATELY as an observation and is never counted as a break
a legal record during a stop is excluded from the break count on purpose — honest history is not misconduct
rules are named from the stored snapshot, so the review says WHICH rule fired
prevented and accepted are kept apart PER RULE, so an unwaivable block is not blurred with an override
a snapshot this app cannot decode is COUNTED as a break and REPORTED unreadable — never dropped, never attributed
a decodable snapshot that names no rule is counted but left UNNAMED rather than attributed to a rule it never carried
another trader’s audit rows are excluded from every number in the payload
an unreadable snapshot is still a break event: the total counts what happened, the rule list counts what could be named
the window filters on the audit’s own day, not on the clock of the read
each day carries its own split and the rules that fired on it, and days are newest-first
the window it actually used is reported, so a review can state the period it covers
reading the tally twice is identical: it is a function of the recorded rows, not of when it was read
a range that is reversed is refused with the module’s own code rather than answered backwards
a date that is not a real UTC day is refused, so a window cannot silently become a different one
an owned user is required: an unowned or absent id is refused rather than answered
the payload refuses to join a break to an outcome, and says why in its own words
the tally cannot influence a grade, a cap, a permission or a guardrail decision, and writes nothing
the basis and scope sentences say what a counted break is and is not, including that an unrecorded break is invisible
an unreadable audit is UNKNOWN, not zero and not a clean week: every count is null and the rule list is empty
an empty but readable audit is a real ZERO with its own shape — distinguishable from the unreadable case above
the same rows give the same answer whether they arrive as a slice or as the whole audit (no hidden global)
the rule parser reads the audit’s stored breach list (and a bare list), deduplicating names within one snapshot
the module is a leaf about the DECISION: neither the guardrail nor the correction bot requires it, so no rule can be crossed because a tally was stale

scope: M12 pure: the guardrail audit, aggregated without inflating it: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
